subject: MAP: Roadtest & capacity reservation lead times
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@atlasdata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Roadtest & capacity reservation lead times

Olivia —

Great talking yesterday. As promised, I’m pulling the initial Mutual Action Plan together so we have a clear path from evaluation -> commit -> provisioning. High level asks and assumptions below; please review and flag anything that’s off.

Summary (proposal):
- Pilot (roadtest): 8-week evaluation using a 16-GPU pool (A100-equivalent) for functional and latency validation.
- Scale tranches: add 32 GPUs (to 48 total) for performance stress tests and early production (phased over 4–6 weeks after pilot).
- Lead times: Dedicated reservation hardware lead time is currently 12–16 weeks from signed reservation for our standard tranche. Private / on-prem can add 4–8 weeks for install/networking depending on site readiness.
- Acceptance: defined perf SLOs (p95 < 120ms on 1k token windows), accuracy regressions < 2% on our eval set, and KV cache warmup validation.
- Fallbacks: short-term burst capacity available through our hosted pool for the first 6 weeks post-commit to avoid cold-start gaps.

Specific asks for Atlas Data:
1) Confirm target commit window (Q3 preferred).
2) Confirm which SKU you consider "A100-equivalent" for sizing (we can map to A10G / H100 variants if needed).
3) Any procurement constraints (PO lead time, internal approvals) we should model into the MAP milestones.

Attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx (draft milestones), capacity_estimate.xlsx (cost & SKU mapping).

If that looks reasonable I’ll convert the MAP to a term sheet and send a DocuSign link for the reservation tranche. Goal: signed reservation by 2026-07-22 to meet a mid-October Dedicated delivery window.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@atlasdata.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atlasdata.com, cto@atlasdata.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 12:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Roadtest & capacity reservation lead times

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear outline. A few clarifying items from our side before we sign off on the MAP:

- SKU mapping: our infra team currently budgets around NVIDIA H100 for model training; for inference we would expect to target a cost-equivalent profile (roughly between A100-40GB and H100 L-variant). Can you give recommended SKU equivalence and delta in unit price?
- Burst: can the hosted burst be constrained to a strict spend cap and throttling policy? Procurement will not sign without explicit guardrails.
- Procurement timing: our finance approval window runs quarterly; I can push for a July 20th approval but need a draft term sheet and PO language this week to brief procurement.
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence and network segmentation checklist are required for our GRC review — we’ll need those artifacts by the time of signing.

I’ve looped in procurement and the CTO for visibility. If we can get a term sheet + SOC 2 artifacts and a clear tranche schedule, we can likely hit that July window for a tranche commitment.

Best,
Olivia Barnes
Head of Product
Atlas Data
olivia.barnes@atlasdata.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Roadtest & capacity reservation lead times

Ben / Soojin —

Looping in the tactical MAP updates based on Olivia’s asks. I’ve sketched a tranche-first plan that reduces procurement risk and shortens initial lead time:

Proposed tranche plan (recommended):
- Tranche 0 (pilot): 16 GPUs — Hosted-managed Dedicated slice — delivered in ~8 weeks via our pre-staged pool. Purpose: functional validation, perf SLO tuning.
- Tranche 1 (early prod): +32 GPUs (48 total) — reserve order placed at signing, phased delivery over 4–6 weeks after pilot acceptance.
- Tranche 2 (scale): +48 GPUs — follow-on reserve to hit steady-state; delivery window 12–16 weeks from tranche 1 order.

SKU guidance: we will map H100/ A100 equivalents in the capacity_estimate.xlsx. Quick rule-of-thumb: treat H100 perf as ~1.4x A100 for throughput; we’ll provide exact token/sec estimates per model.

Procurement guardrails (to address finance concerns):
- Spend cap for hosted-burst: hard limit in the MAP (example: $10k/month) with automatic throttling and alerting.
- Term sheet includes a 30-day soft exit window (reduced early-termination fees for initial pilot tranche).
- SOC 2 & network segmentation package: attaching acceptance_tests.md and a summary artifact; full SOC 2 report will be provided via secure link upon NDA acknowledgment.

Next steps I’ll take this morning:
1) Update MAP_v1.xlsx -> MAP_v1.1 with tranche schedule and milestone dates.
2) Generate a short term sheet (one pager) and send DocuSign for the tranche 0 reservation.
3) Add explicit billing/PO language for procurement.

Attachments I’m adding: tranche_schedule.csv, acceptance_tests.md. I’ll also drop a DocuSign link in the next email.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199

This looks good and addresses the key procurement concerns. Procurement has reviewed the draft tranche approach and asked that the DocuSign term sheet include PO wiring instructions and the spend cap language you noted.

We’re ready to sign tranche 0 (16 GPUs) pending the DocuSign term sheet. Procurement will route the PO after signing; I’ve attached a preliminary PO here (PO_Atlas_13872.pdf stub). Our internal target: sign DocuSign by 2026-06-18, kickoff roadtest week of 2026-06-22.
